1. Project Overview & The Household Problem in India

Indian households manage life's most essential responsibilities across fragile, disconnected silos. Important documents (Aadhaar, PAN, property titles, insurance policies) are scattered across physical paper files, WhatsApp messages, and forgotten email attachments. Utility bills and EMIs lapse quietly, incurring recurring late fees. In medical emergencies, family members scramble in panic to find blood groups, allergies, and prescriptions.

🚨 The ₹5,00,000 Crisis Panic

When an urgent emergency hits (medical hospitalization, pandemic crisis, accident), families need instant liquid funds (e.g. ₹5 Lakhs). With savings fragmented across child education, car funds, and house deposits, families panic and make irreversible financial mistakes.

🛡️ The SAHAY Solution

SAHAY centralizes all documents, health vitals, daily obligations, and goal vaults into one role-governed OS. It turns passive files into active timelines with predictive life-event alerts, zero-knowledge encryption, and crisis liquidation intelligence.

System Architecture & Component Overview

Tier Technologies Core Responsibility
Presentation React 19, TypeScript, Vite 5, Tailwind CSS Responsive, accessible light-theme web shell with role-aware views.
Edge & Gateway Nginx 1.31 (Alpine), AWS EC2 Reverse proxies port 80 to FastAPI backend and serves static SPA assets.
Backend API FastAPI 0.115, Python 3.12, Uvicorn (ASGI) Asynchronous REST API, cryptographic JWT tokens, schema validation.
Database Tier PostgreSQL 16 (pgvector), SQLAlchemy 2.0 35 production relational tables enforcing multi-tenant isolation.
Security Core AES-256-GCM, Bcrypt, PyJWT Zero-knowledge document encryption, PII masking, immutable audit log.
AI Engine Google Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite, Async RAG Household context ingestion, natural language queries, visual tables.

3. Mathematical & Algorithmic Formulation

3.1 Crisis Emergency Mode: The ₹5,00,000 Liquidation Optimizer

When an unexpected medical or pandemic emergency requires ₹5,00,000 immediately, SAHAY executes a deterministic liquidation strategy:

Liquidation Priority Hierarchy:
Tier 1: Emergency Reserve Vault (0% penalty, instant transfer)
Tier 2: Discretionary Goals (e.g., Vacation, Luxury Gadget — zero tax penalty)
Tier 3: Long-term Asset Goals (e.g., Car Downpayment — deferrable purchase)
Tier 4: Protected Sacred Goals (e.g., Child Education, House Deed — NEVER liquidated)
Post-Crisis Replenishment Formula:
Monthly Free Surplus (S) = Monthly Income (I) - [Rent (R) + Groceries (G) + Utilities (U) + Expenses (E)]
With I = ₹85,000 and Living Expenses = ₹40,000, S = ₹45,000/month.
Replenishment Horizon (T) = Target Amount (₹5,00,000) / Monthly Surplus (₹45,000) = 11.1 Months.

4. AWS Cloud Deployment & Local Setup

4.1 Production Cloud Architecture

The application is deployed on an AWS EC2 instance running Ubuntu 24.04 LTS:

  • Public IPv4 Endpoint: http://16.178.56.236/
  • API Swagger Documentation: http://16.178.56.236/docs
  • Reverse Proxy: Nginx 1.31 Alpine managing gzip compression, SPA routing, and upstream proxying to backend:8000.
  • Container Topology: 4 Docker containers (sahay_frontend, sahay_backend, sahay_postgres, sahay_redis) interconnected on an internal bridge network.

4.2 Local Reproduction Commands

# 1. Clone & Setup git clone https://github.com/ndheeraj-shetty/sahay.git cd sahay # 2. Start Backend cd backend python -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate # On Windows: .venv\Scriptsctivate pip install -r requirements.txt python -m uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 # 3. Start Frontend (in separate terminal) cd ../frontend npm install npm run dev # Launches Vite dev server at http://localhost:5173
